newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle priced at $69 for next week-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle priced at $69 for next week-trade.

text.p: High Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet Friday and feedlot sources said much of next week's offerings will be priced at $69.00 per cwt, $2.00 higher than this week's sales.

Cattle in Kansas and Oklahoma had been stressed by cold, damp conditions early this week and then by snow, ice and high winds late Thursday and early Friday. Some feedlots reported the weather slowed cattle weight gains, with cattle shipped Friday weighing less than expected.
High winds and ice knocked out electrical power at near Garden City, Kan., late Thursday and early Friday.
Power was restored Friday but the wind was still strong late in the day, feedlot sources there said.
Sharply higher cash beef prices late this week coupled with strong gains in CME live cattle futures had feedlot managers optimistic of receiving higher cattle prices next week.
At midday Friday, USDA reported cutout value for choice 700/850 lb carcasses was $101.47 per cwt versus $99.25 Wednesday.
